newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria short-term deposit rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria short-term deposit rates fall.

text.p: Bulgarian short-term interbank deposit rates fell on Monday in line with a main interest rate cut and due to the lack of demand for funds, dealers said.
"There is no demand for interbank deposits as banks' liquidity is very high," said a bank dealer.
The central bank cut its simple annual main interest rate to 9.76 percent from 10.12 percent, in force from Monday.
Traders said that banks' liquidity improved due to foreign currency selling to the central bank after the introduction of a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 levs per mark last Tuesday.
Banks which have bought marks at lower levels in the past several weeks sold them to the central bank to profit from forex transaction costs.
The central bank was buying marks at 995 levs and selling at 1,000 levs under the currency board system.
Traders said that commercial banks held their free lev funds at their accounts with the central bank.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Friday that from July 14 it would stop paying interest on these accounts and on banks' minimum required reserves due to a fall in BNB income under the currency board.

A commercial banker said on Friday the BNB would cut the interest on banks' accounts and banks' minimum reserves to 2.61 percent and 3.86 percent respectively this week from 2.7 and 4.0 percent a week ago.

Overnight interbank depo rates fell to 5-6 percent annually from 9-10 percent on Friday, while deposits for up to seven days were borrowed at a simple annual interest of 7-8 percent, flat from Friday.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 8.00 percent on Friday from 9.50 percent on Thursday, a central bank official said.
